key_insight: A convolutional information-theoretic model isolates vortical structures that are most causally linked to a chosen future aerodynamic quantity, revealing when vortex cores and shear layers become dynamically important during extreme gust–airfoil interaction.
engineering_relevance: This enables physics-guided flow-feature discovery for transient aerodynamic design and diagnosis, helping engineers focus on the structures that drive lift response or energy transfer in unsteady gust encounters.
method: Decompose each flow snapshot into informative and residual components based on contribution to a future target variable.
Use convolutional information-theoretic learning to identify causally important vortical structures.
Compare extracted structures for different future variables, including lift coefficient and scale-dependent energy transfer.
evidence_signal: On a turbulent wake–extreme vortex gust interaction at Reynolds number 5000, the method highlighted vortex cores before impingement and shear layers after massive separation, with patterns consistent with instantaneous force-element analysis.
watch_item: The extracted structures depend on the chosen future target and training setup, so interpretation may vary across flow cases, time horizons, and model generalization settings.
paper_title: Extracting informative vortical structures of turbulent wake-extreme vortex gust interactions with machine learning
